subject: Aurora Health pricing check + commitment options
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Liang <tom.liang@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + ask: token volumes & commitment targets (post-demo)

Hi Sarah / Tom — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our side and a couple of things we need so we can finalize a committed pricing option for Aurora.

Call highlights (very short):
- Primary workloads: clinical note summarization + patient Q&A (bursting at day-end).
- Expected steady-state: ~8–12M tokens/day (billing tokens) with peaks to ~25M tokens/day.
- Latency target: 200–350ms p50 for single-turn generation.

What we need from you to finalize options:
1) Confirm a 12-month vs 24-month preferred commitment window (helps price multi-year incentives).
2) Target committed volume (monthly or annual) you would be comfortable committing to — e.g., 50M, 100M, 250M tokens/month (we can show tiered pricing).
3) Ballpark target cost goal per $/1M tokens (so we can align discounts). If you have a target unit economics, share it — we typically see customers aiming for $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model/quantization.

Attached is a draft proposal and a simple usage estimate sheet (placeholder numbers). I pulled together two example commitment packages (see attachment):
- Option A (12mo, 100M/mo): $1,200 per 1M tokens pre-discount
- Option B (24mo, 150M/mo): $1,050 per 1M tokens pre-discount

We can layer a startup credit package and/or committed-use discount on top. To make the official commercial, we need your preferred commit band + whether procurement wants an initial pilot credit to apply against month 1.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three items above by EOD Wed (or tell us a good time to sync), we’ll get a formal DocuSign-ready quote over to procurement.

Thanks —
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0188

Cc: Tom Liang <tom.liang@aurorahealth.com>, Aurora Health Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: token volumes & commitment targets (post-demo)

Hi Monica — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

1) Commitment window: Preference toward 24 months if pricing moves materially. Short-term pilot for first 30 days then full commit.
2) Target committed volume: We're comfortable discussing 100M–150M tokens / month as a starting negotiation band (clinical notes + search + embeddings). Monthly variability expected but want a predictable SLO on unit cost.
3) Cost goal: We’d like to land around $800–$900 per 1M tokens (target). If committed + multi-year incentives can reach that, we can accelerate procurement.

Procurement (cc’d) will need a clear breakdown of committed vs overage pricing and any minimum monthly spend. Tom, can procurement review the attachments and flag any standard T&Cs we need?

If you can return two concrete commercial options (12mo vs 24mo) with the $/1M after discounts and any startup credit, we’ll queue review with procurement this week.

Thanks —
Sarah Gomez
Head of AI Products | Aurora Health
sarah.gomez@aurorahealth.com

Monica / Laura — internal note after quick pricing review. DO NOT SEND AS-IS TO CUSTOMER until we align on one front.

Summary suggestions:
- Baseline model: assume pre-discount unit $1,200 / 1M tokens (matches Option A in doc).
- Committed-use discount tiers: 10% @ 50M/mo, 20% @ 100M/mo, 25% @ 150M/mo.
- Multi-year incentive: additional 8–12% credit applied as pre-paid invoice credit when customer signs 24mo (scale by band).
- Startup program: we can offer a first-60-day 50% credit on usage up to 10M tokens to accelerate proof-of-value.

Quick margin check: at 20% discount on 100M/mo, blended $960 / 1M tokens — still holds margin if we recommend quantized model variants (NLP-small/Q4HF) for inference. If customer insists on $800 / 1M for 100M/mo 24mo, we need to apply a multi-year incentive + 5% engineering implementation credit to preserve core margin.

Hi Sarah / Procurement team — per our internal review I’m sending two formal commercial options. I also included the startup credit and a multi-year incentive scenario. Summary below; full details are in the attached proposal and the DocuSign link at the bottom.

Option 1 — 12 months (100M tokens / month commit)
- Pre-discount list price: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Committed-use discount: 20% -> $960 per 1M tokens
- Startup credit: 50% credit on first 60 days up to 10M tokens
- Overage: $1,050 per 1M tokens
- Estimated annual spend (100M/mo): ~$1,152,000

Option 2 — 24 months (150M tokens / month commit) — recommended for target $/1M
- Pre-discount list price: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Committed-use discount: 25% -> $900 per 1M tokens
- Multi-year incentive (24mo): additional 10% invoice credit applied as pre-paid credit -> effective $810 per 1M tokens on committed volume in year 1 (accounting for incentive)
- Startup credit: 50% credit on first 60 days up to 10M tokens
- Overage: $950 per 1M tokens
- Estimated annual spend (150M/mo): ~$1,458,000 (year-1 effective cost reduced by incentive credit)

Notes on unit economics and next steps:
- The 24mo option hits your stated target range ($800–$900 / 1M) once the multi-year incentive is layered in. If Aurora needs to land at $800 flat, we should discuss an additional implementation credit (one-time) or a higher committed band.
- Overage tiers are structured to preserve predictable SLOs during peaks.

Requested confirmation from Aurora: please confirm which option (1 or 2) you prefer and whether procurement wants any specific T&C redlines before we generate the DocuSign. If you confirm Option 2, we’ll prepare a 24mo DocuSign with the incentive language and a simple SOW for onboarding/workshops.
